title: Privilege Heattrail & Access Review — prototype for contextual RBAC and audit UX
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Admins and compliance reviewers need an at-a-glance, searchable view that explains who had access to sensitive resources, why the access changed, and which deploys/rollouts or support sessions correlated with privilege changes. Existing audit pages are verbose chronological logs that are hard to filter by intent, scope, or cost impact.

Goal: Deliver a design prototype that surfaces a compact, queryable "Heattrail" (temporal heatmap + event stream) combined with a contextual access-review flow. The prototype should cover: multi-workspace rollups, role vs. entitlement views, action replay (recreate reviewer context), exportable evidence bundles, and a lightweight moderator workflow for approving or rolling back policy changes.
acceptance_criteria: Heattrail view prototype (desktop) that visualizes access intensity per workspace/resource over last 90 days
Event stream panes that link each change to originating actor (user/service), PR/Runbook, and deploy/rollout IDs
Contextual review modal where reviewer can annotate, mark as accepted/revoke access, and schedule a rollback playbook
Exportable evidence package (PDF + CSV) containing filtered events, screenshots, and linked PR/Confluence references
Design tokens and component spec for timeline, heatmap swatches, and reviewer controls delivered for Dev handoff
Accessibility audit checklist completed for color contrast and keyboard interactions
Prototype usability test (5 sessions) with internal SRE/security reviewers and consolidated findings

decisions: Keep default retention at 90 days for Heattrail to balance cost and utility; provide configurability for Enterprise to extend to 2 years via Private settings.
Expose a single-click 'revoke & notify' action but gate it behind role checks and an undo window (5 minutes) to prevent accidental privilege removal.

Rank events by 'review priority' using a heuristic combining scope (number of affected resources), actor risk (external contractor/service), and correlated cost spike. This score surfaces at the top of the event card.
Export evidence bundles will include event CSV, snapshot JSON, linked PR/Confluence URLs, and an autogenerated narrative explaining the access change (drafted copy in PRD).
tradeoffs: Verbosity vs. Signal: Showing full raw logs is comprehensive but noisy. We prioritize synthesized 'evidence' cards with on-demand raw log access to keep the interface scannable.

On-client rendering complexity for heatmap vs server-side aggregation: prefer pre-aggregated rollups to reduce client CPU on low-powered admin machines; requires backend support for rolling summaries.
Immediate revoke UX vs safety: to keep operations safe we add undo and require a reason/comment for forced revokes which adds friction but improves auditability.
risks: Data volume: heatmap and rollup queries may be expensive for large orgs; need quotas or sample rates to prevent runaway cost.
Misleading signal: heuristic scoring could deprioritize true incidents if actor/context signals are noisy; will need iterative tuning with security team.
Privacy: exposing too much contextual info in export bundles could leak sensitive identifiers; export should mask PII by default and require explicit permission to include unmasked values.
